meta.title: CPC Utils — CPC 7z SFX Builder and CPC MInst Launcher
meta.description: CPC Utils makes portable Windows tools: CPC 7z SFX Builder for self-extracting 7-Zip packages and CPC MInst Launcher for Windows and WinPE. Free download, no .NET, no runtime.

hero.sub: CPC 7z SFX Builder turns a folder or an archive into one self-extracting exe: choose what runs, where it unpacks, and what happens after. CPC MInst Launcher carries the same profile from Windows into WinPE.

umbrella.h2: Two tools today, one brand for the next ones
umbrella.p: Every CPC Utils product is a single portable executable with no runtime dependencies, so it behaves the same on a clean Windows install, a technician's WinPE stick, or an everyday desktop.

spotlight.p: The source is scanned once and every executable is listed with its folder in front of the name. Typing filters the list in place; arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home/End and Enter work the way you expect. The header always shows how many matches you have out of how many files.

spotlight.pb: Switch it on and the same package gets a wizard, a target folder, desktop and Start menu shortcuts and an uninstall entry. Switch it off and you are back to a plain portable package.

items.q: Does CPC 7z SFX Builder need .NET or an installation?
items.a: No. It is one portable exe that talks to the Windows API directly. Copy it to a USB drive or a network share and run it.

items.q: Does CPC MInst Launcher work in WinPE?
items.a: Yes. It uses the same profile in Windows and in WinPE, so technicians carry one set of launch items instead of two.
Signing the output with your own certificate is supported. Without a certificate Windows shows the usual warning; payload binding still detects later modification.

items.q: What does a package from CPC 7z SFX Builder contain?
items.a: An extraction stub, your compressed files, and a configuration block. Optionally a signature and a payload hash.
In a profile file next to the exe, or in the folder you choose. The tools read the registry for environment detection only.

sfx-builder.title: CPC 7z SFX Builder — visual self-extracting package builder
sfx-builder.lead: A visual editor for 7-Zip self-extracting packages: choose the source, decide how it unpacks and what it runs, then build one exe.

sections.p: Every executable in the source appears once, root files first, with the folder shown in front of the name. Typing filters the list as you go.
Choose the program to start, optional parameters, a finish message, and preparation scripts that run after extraction in the order you picked.
Temp, LocalAppData, AppData, ProgramData or next to the package. Deleting the files after the run is a separate switch on purpose.
Add a wizard, a target folder, desktop and Start menu shortcuts, and an uninstall entry — or keep it as a plain portable package.
The built package can carry a signature and a payload hash. The Check page reports configuration, content, stub and integrity separately.

closing.p: Source, behaviour, installer options and verification live in the same project - no export, no second tool.

launcher.title: CPC MInst Launcher - one tool list for Windows and WinPE
launcher.lead: The program list a service bench actually needs: your tools grouped and searchable, one click from launch. The same profile works in Windows and in WinPE - no installer, no runtime, no console windows.

heroShot.alt: CPC MInst Launcher showing a WinPE profile: grouped tool list, search field, tool sidebar and the info bar of the selected program

sections.p: Tools are organised into groups - Backup and Restore, Hard Disk, Diagnostics - that you can create, rename, reorder, sort A-Z or hide. Nothing depends on where a file happens to sit on disk.
Start typing and the list narrows immediately, without pressing Enter. Backspace widens it again. Groups collapse to the matches, so a 200-item stick still takes two keystrokes.

The profile switch at the top swaps the whole list: load, duplicate, rename, delete, import or export. Profiles are MInstAll-compatible .ini files, so an existing collection does not have to be rebuilt.

Items can be flagged PE-only or 64-bit-only, and the ones marked autorun run in order when the launcher is started with --autorun, skipping anything whose OS does not match. Settings that make no sense in PE - starting with Windows, for one - are disabled instead of silently failing.

Every save writes a backup first; if the backup cannot be written, nothing is saved and you are told why. Deleting an item asks whether the file goes too, and the shortcuts generated for it are removed with it.
Each item takes its icon from the program itself or from the icon library, and can create a desktop or Start menu shortcut. Start folder and arguments are optional extras.

spotlight.alt: Three partition tools left after typing partition: the search filters the grouped list while the info bar shows size, path and platform
spotlight.h: Two keystrokes instead of a scroll
spotlight.p: Filtering happens on the list you already have, not in a new window: type a few letters, watch the groups collapse to the matching tools, and the info bar tells you the size, the path behind the {Patch} token and whether the item is 32-bit, 64-bit or both.

About 730 KB, settings in ui.dat next to it, no .NET and no runtime to install.

items.a: The item stays in the list marked as not found, with its path in the info bar, so a broken stick is visible before a client is sitting next to it.
